requirement_text: In 2026-2027, Columbia is test-optional for applicants to Columbia College and Columbia Engineering. ... There are no minimum test score requirements for admission. Students applying to enter Columbia in Fall 2027 (ie. applicants in the 2026-2027 admissions cycle) may choose whether or not to submit testing.
limitations: Applies to first-year and transfer applicants to Columbia College and Columbia Engineering only (not Columbia's other schools).
researcher_notes: Corroborated by a second, separately-published official page (Testing Policy Update, published Friday, June 12, 2026: 'Columbia College and Columbia Engineering will remain test optional for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle.'). Testing Policy page itself carries 'Updated on Monday, June 8, 2026.' Both pages agree; no conflict between them. This is the CURRENT policy governing the admissions cycle open for applications as of the 2026-08-21 retrieval date. 'Admissions cycle' year here = application/decision year; entry year is one year later (2026-2027 cycle -> Fall 2027 entry), consistent with the adjacent 'First-year applications for Fall 2027 are now available' statement on the firstyear page.

requirement_text: Starting in August 2027, Columbia College and Columbia Engineering will require first-year and transfer students to submit standardized test results from the ACT or SAT as part of their application for admission. You may choose to take either the ACT or the SAT. If reporting the ACT, you will need to include your scores from English, Math, and Reading sections, as well as the Composite Score. The Science and Writing sections are optional. If reporting the SAT, you will need to include Evidenced-Based Reading, Writing and Math sections.
researcher_notes: Corroborated by the Testing Policy Update page (published 2026-06-12): 'effective August 2027 for the 2027-2028 admissions cycle. First-year and transfer applicants seeking to enroll for Fall 2028 will need to submit either SAT or ACT scores.' cycle_year=2028 is the entry year (Fall 2028), consistent with the record contract's 'cycle_year is the ENTRY year' rule -- the '2027-2028 admissions cycle' label itself is the application/decision year pair, not the entry year.

requirement_text: Students who have not taken the ACT or the SAT may request a testing requirement exception if they face challenges in meeting the testing policy outlined above. A testing waiver may be requested at the time of your application if personal circumstances such as financial or personal hardship, lack of access to testing locations, or natural disaster or community disruption inhibit your ability to take the ACT or the SAT. Students who request the waiver will not be at a disadvantage in our process.
researcher_notes: Applies once testing becomes required (2027-2028 admissions cycle / Fall 2028 entry onward); not applicable while the current test-optional policy (REQ0001) is in force.

requirement_text: As of March 1, 2023, Columbia is test-optional for applicants to Columbia College or Columbia Engineering. Columbia is extending our test-optional policy for two years, effective for first-year and transfer applicants to Columbia College or Columbia Engineering for entrance in Fall 2023 and Fall 2024. ... After a period of review and synthesis, our testing policy will be re-assessed for the 2024-2025 application cycle.
limitations: Page is stale/historical relative to the current cycle but remains live at this URL as of retrieval (2026-08-21); the older URL undergrad.admissions.columbia.edu/node/2067 301-redirects to this same page. Explicitly self-scopes to Fall 2023 and Fall 2024 entry and names its own re-assessment date (2024-2025 cycle), so it does not claim current applicability -- classified VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rather than CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE. Superseded by REQ-2026-08-21-COL0001 (current 2026-2027 cycle policy) and REQ-2026-08-21-COL0002 (2027-2028 cycle onward).
researcher_notes: Announcement posted November 24, 2021; 'Details for applicants' section posted July 6, 2022. This is exactly the 'stale test-optional page still live' pattern the research brief asked to watch for. Recorded deliberately (per project convention that VERIFIED_HISTORICAL rows are not noise) so a later pass does not rediscover this URL and mistake its Fall-2023/2024 content for current policy. See REQ-2026-08-21-COL0001 for the current, authoritative testing policy.

requirement_text: For exams taken on or before January 20, 2026, a minimum score of 105 on the internet-based test (iBT) of the TOEFL is necessary for admission to Columbia. Your score must be reported directly to Columbia by the testing service, using report code 2116. Columbia accepts only TOEFL iBT® scores by test administration date (e.g. full test administration results for one sitting) and does not accept MyBest™ scores. We will accept online results from the TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition. You may send multiple results.
limitations: Threshold is gated by test-taken date (on/before 2026-01-20), not by admissions cycle -- a pre-cutover score can still be submitted by an applicant in the current cycle if within its normal validity window. Published under the 'International Applicants' section; text itself is framed around demonstrating English proficiency, not citizenship, so may also apply to some domestic applicants from non-English-instruction backgrounds.
researcher_notes: Named exclusion (per this project's known trap pattern): Columbia does NOT accept TOEFL MyBest (superscored) results -- only single-administration score reports. A numerically qualifying MyBest composite must NOT be evaluated as 'met' -- mirrors the Edinburgh One-Skill-Retake / Koc superscore exclusions documented elsewhere in this research project. Companion record REQ-2026-08-21-COL0006 carries the post-cutover (1-6 scale) threshold from the same source paragraph; both are unambiguous because the source page itself states both scales with the exact ETS cutover date (2026-01-21), unlike the Glasgow/Bogazici cases found elsewhere in this project.

requirement_text: For exams taken on or after January 21, 2026, a minimum score of 5.5 is necessary [on the TOEFL iBT, for admission to Columbia]. Your score must be reported directly to Columbia by the testing service, using report code 2116.
limitations: Bracketed words supplied for readability; original sentence continues directly from the pre-cutover sentence in REQ-2026-08-21-COL0005 on the source page and elides the repeated subject.
researcher_notes: Overall-score threshold only; the source page states no per-subtest minimum, so (unlike the Glasgow case documented elsewhere in this project) there is no partially-unsatisfiable subtest component here. 5.5 on the new 1-6 average scale (in 0.5 increments per ETS) is the direct successor to the legacy 105/120 threshold in REQ-2026-08-21-COL0005.

requirement_text: A minimum score of 7.5 on the IELTS is necessary for admission to Columbia. Your score must be reported directly to Columbia Undergraduate Admissions by the testing service.
researcher_notes: IELTS 0-9 band scale is unaffected by the January 2026 TOEFL rescale (confirmed unaffected in this project's cross-university scale audit).

requirement_text: A minimum score of 135 on the current DET is necessary for admission to Columbia. Your score must be reported directly to Columbia Undergraduate Admissions by the testing service.
researcher_notes: Official figure is 135. Several third-party aggregator sites (Clastify, Ambitio, CollegeVine) report 125 instead -- those are not used here; the official page's live figure (135) is authoritative. DET has no corresponding value in this project's test_scale enum (TOEFL/IELTS/SAT/Cambridge only), so left null rather than forced into a mismatched category.

requirement_text: A minimum score of 191 on the current C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency Cambridge English Exams is necessary for admission to Columbia. Your score must be reported directly to Columbia Undergraduate Admissions by the testing service.

There are several different ways to demonstrate that you are proficient in English on your application without an English Language Proficiency exam: Your home language is English. Your primary language of instruction at school has been English for the duration of your secondary school career. You earned one or more of the following subsection scores on the SAT or ACT: 700 or higher on the Reading and Writing section of the SAT (either paper or digital administration); 29 or higher on the English or Reading sections of the ACT.
limitations: test_scale/scale_ambiguity describe only the SAT-subscore pathway (700+ on Reading & Writing, 1600-scale, unaffected by any rescale); the home-language and instruction-language pathways are not scaled tests.
researcher_notes: If a student meets any one of these criteria, none of the exams in REQ0005/0006/0007/0008/0009 need be submitted.

requirement_text: (Optional) Applicants to Columbia can elect to send InitialView or Vericant videos to emphasize language fluency. These videos should be scheduled, completed and submitted to Columbia by November 15 for Early Decision, January 15 for Regular Decision or March 1 for Transfer applicants.
limitations: '(Optional)' prefix added by researcher for clarity; not itself part of the source sentence, but the surrounding source paragraph is unambiguous that this is elective ('can elect to send'), not required.
researcher_notes: Optional supplementary evidence of spoken English fluency, distinct from and in addition to the pass/fail English Language Proficiency exams in REQ0005-0009. Companion deadline records: DL-2026-08-21-COL0016 (ED) and DL-2026-08-21-COL0017 (RD).

requirement_text: Columbia accepts all secondary school curricula (e.g., International Baccalaureate, Cambridge A Levels, National School curricula, etc.), and applications are reviewed within the context of your curriculum.

Internal and external exam results—such as A Level, International Baccalaureate, French Baccalaureate, Advanced Placement (AP) exams, and other final national exam results—must be submitted if they are required to complete and graduate from secondary school. If they are not required for the completion of and graduation from secondary school, you are not required to submit results. Advanced Placement (AP) and other optional standardized exam scores are not required by Columbia, but we will accept your results if you choose to submit them.
researcher_notes: Named-inclusion / conditional rule, not a blanket yes/no: whether A-Level/IB/French Bac/other national exam results are 'required' for a given applicant depends on that student's own secondary-school graduation requirements, which a generic evaluator cannot determine from the university side alone. AP itself is always optional at Columbia regardless of the student's school. Same substance corroborated on the International Applicants page (INTL_APPLY).

requirement_text: Columbia requires two teacher recommendations. These recommendations must come from teachers who taught you in academic disciplines.

program_name: Columbia Engineering (The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science)
requirement_text: For applicants to Columbia Engineering, one of the teacher recommendations must come from a math or science teacher.
researcher_notes: Overlay on the university-wide 2-teacher-recommendation baseline in REQ-2026-08-21-COL0014; applies to Columbia Engineering applicants only, not Columbia College.

requirement_text: Secondary School Report: An official high school transcript from all high schools attended. One high school counselor's recommendation and school profile. The completed midyear report.
researcher_notes: Bundles transcript + counselor recommendation + school profile + midyear report under Columbia's own 'Secondary School Report' heading; condensed from a bulleted list on the source page into one sentence per bullet, wording otherwise unchanged.

requirement_text: Interviews are not a part of the application process. ... Applicants who are candidates for admission through the Higher Education Opportunity Program and National Opportunity Program will be offered the chance to speak with current student volunteers to inform them about the nature of that particular admission process and advising program. These are counseling conversations rather than evaluative interviews.
researcher_notes: Page references 'the announcement from May 18, 2023' as the origin of this policy: Columbia discontinued its alumni-interview program (run via the Alumni Representative Committee) effective the 2023-2024 admissions cycle, citing application volume. Checked for a stale page still advertising live alumni interviews (same class of trap as the testing-policy stale pages); none found still live in this pass -- only the current 'Interviews' page and third-party retrospective commentary were found.

requirement_text: [Application includes:] Autobiographical information. Lists and descriptions of a student's achievements, activities, employment and summer activities. Personal essay.
researcher_notes: This is the standard Common Application / Coalition Application on Scoir personal statement, administered by the application platform rather than being Columbia-specific; exact prompts and word limits are set by Common App / Coalition, not reproduced here. Distinct from the Columbia-specific writing supplement in REQ-2026-08-21-COL0019.

requirement_text: 2026-2027 Columbia-Specific Questions. For the list question: 100 word maximum -- 'List the titles of texts, resources and outlets that have contributed to your intellectual development outside of academic courses, including but not limited to books, journals, websites, podcasts, essays, plays, presentations, videos, museums and other content that you enjoy.' For each of six short answer questions, respond in 150 words or fewer: (1) 'Tell us about an aspect of your life so far or your lived experience that is important to you, and describe how it has shaped the way you would learn from and contribute to Columbia's multidimensional and collaborative environment.' (2) '...describe a time when you did not agree with someone and discuss how you engaged with them and what you took away from the interaction.' (3) '...describe a situation in which you have navigated through adversity and discuss how you changed as a result.' (4) 'Why are you interested in attending Columbia University?' (5) 'What attracts you to your preferred areas of study at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering?'
limitations: Source page enumerates 'six short answer questions' in its instructions but the fetched question list itself contains the 100-word list question plus five 150-word short answers (five, not six) -- recorded as fetched; possible the instructions text is templated/reused from a prior year with a different question count and was not fully updated, or a sixth conditional question renders only after selecting an academic program on the live form and was not captured by a static fetch. Treat the question count as NEEDS_REVIEW-adjacent; the quoted prompts themselves are verbatim and reliable.
researcher_notes: Page explicitly dated 'Updated Tuesday, July 28, 2026' -- recent and reliable, current for the 2026-2027 cycle. Will very likely change for the 2027-2028 cycle; do not treat as evergreen. A third-party blog (not used as a source here) additionally claims a 50-word 'why study in the US' question exists for some applicant subgroup; this was not found on the fetched static page and is NOT included in requirement_text -- flagging only, not recorded as fact.

requirement_text: Columbia College has no explicit number of unit requirements for admission, but applicants must present evidence that they are prepared for college work in the humanities, mathematics, social sciences, foreign languages and natural sciences. Accordingly, Columbia College strongly recommends the following secondary school preparation: Four years of English literature and composition; Four years of mathematics—unless you have already completed what is available at your school; Three to four years of history and/or social studies; Three to four years of laboratory science; Three to four years of one world language (ancient or modern) taken during high school.
researcher_notes: Explicitly 'strongly recommends,' not a mandatory unit count ('no explicit number of unit requirements') -- must not be evaluated as a hard pass/fail eligibility gate.

program_name: Columbia Engineering (The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science)
requirement_text: The School of Engineering and Applied Science prescribes no standardized course of study for secondary school students applying for first-year admission. However, the Engineering curriculum is heavily driven by physics and calculus, so Columbia Engineering strongly advises these courses within the following recommended academic preparation: Four years of mathematics through calculus—unless you have already completed what is available at your school; Four years of laboratory science, including one year of chemistry and one year of physics—preferably in the last two years of secondary school; Four years of English literature and composition; Three to four years of history and/or social studies; Two to three years of a world language (ancient or modern) taken during high school.
researcher_notes: Explicitly 'strongly advises,' not mandatory ('prescribes no standardized course of study'). Differs from Columbia College (REQ0020) in specificity: mathematics through calculus explicitly named, lab science specifies 1 yr chemistry + 1 yr physics, world language range is 2-3 yrs vs Columbia College's 3-4 yrs.

requirement_text: All applicants who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States, as well as students granted refugee visas by the United States, DACA recipients and undocumented students, are read in a need-blind manner, no matter where they attend school or where they reside. ... All other applicants are evaluated in a need-aware manner, which means that the admissions committee takes into consideration how much financial aid a student requires when rendering an admissions decision. Columbia is committed to meeting the full need of all applicants admitted as first-year, transfer and Combined Plan students, regardless of citizenship.
researcher_notes: This is the single most important international-applicant admissions-policy fact for ORYN's international-student user base. Independently corroborated in substance (not verbatim-identical wording) on two further official Columbia subdomains: https://cc-seas.financialaid.columbia.edu/how/aid/works ('Admission to Columbia is need-blind for US Citizens and Eligible Noncitizens... Undocumented students who reside in the United States are also evaluated in a need-blind manner') and https://cc-seas.financialaid.columbia.edu/eligibility/myths ('Columbia is not need-blind for international / non-domestic students. However, if you are admitted, and you demonstrate financial need, Columbia will meet your full need for all four years of study.'). No conflict found across the three pages; all agree on the same substantive rule.

requirement_text: United States citizens are considered domestic applicants for the purpose of financial aid, and, as such, are always reviewed in a need-blind manner.
researcher_notes: Clarifies that need-blind/need-aware status in REQ-2026-08-21-COL0022 turns on citizenship/immigration status, not on country of residence or school location.

requirement_text: International students are welcome to apply Early Decision. However, even very competitive international candidates who are applying for financial aid and fall out of the “need-blind” category may be deferred to Regular Decision so the Committee on Admissions can review the entire global applicant pool.
researcher_notes: Practical consequence of the need-aware policy (REQ0022) specifically within the binding Early Decision round (see REQ0028): an international financial-aid applicant is not guaranteed a December ED decision and may be held for the Regular Decision pool.

requirement_text: International applicants must indicate their plan to apply for financial aid when submitting their admission application. If admitted without requesting financial aid, international students may not change their status to apply for aid, even if their financial circumstances change. International financial aid cannot be awarded in subsequent years if not awarded at the time of admission.
limitations: A narrow exception exists per a separate official page (Myths about Financial Aid): 'An international student whose family experiences a severe and unforeseen change in circumstances may apply for financial aid at any time, and such requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis,' though that same page also states Columbia 'cannot guarantee' aid in that scenario.
researcher_notes: Applies to international / non-domestic applicants for financial aid purposes as defined in REQ0022 (i.e., not US citizens/permanent residents/refugee-visa holders/DACA/undocumented).

requirement_text: CSS Profile ... Available October 1, 2026. Our CSS School Code is 2116 and is listed as “Columbia U: College & Engineering”. NOTE: There are several school codes for Columbia University. Students applying to Columbia College or The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science MUST choose the school code 2116, or your application materials will not be received. Complete the 2027-2028 CSS Profile online if you wish to apply for Columbia University Grant. Sending your CSS Profile to one college costs $25; additional reports are $16 per college. If this cost presents a significant financial burden for your family, please email us to learn about the fee waiver approval process. Columbia requires the CSS Profile for both biological or adoptive parents.
limitations: Identical content (dates, code, fee) independently confirmed on the parallel RD-International, ED-Domestic and RD-Domestic versions of this page; CSS Profile mechanics do not differ by round or by domestic/international status, only the financial-aid application deadline itself does (see DL-2026-08-21-COL0003/0005).
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT NAMING-CONVENTION TRAP, flagged for the other parallel US-market research agents too: Columbia's financial-aid subdomain (cc-seas.financialaid.columbia.edu) labels CSS Profile pages by ACADEMIC/AID YEAR OF ENROLLMENT ('27-28' = student enrolled Fall 2027-Spring 2028), which is offset by one from the admissions subdomain's 'admissions cycle' label ('2026-2027 admissions cycle' = apply now, enter Fall 2027). The two labels actually refer to the SAME cohort once translated (both mean Fall 2027 entry), but a naive literal string match of '2026-2027' against the finaid site would incorrectly select the '26-27 CSS Profile' page instead -- which is for the PRIOR cohort (Fall 2026 entry, i.e. students already enrolling around now, retrieved 2026-08-21). Verified this distinction directly: the '26-27' page states 'Available October 1, 2025' and 'Complete the 2026-2027 CSS Profile,' while the '27-28' page (used as this record's source) states 'Available October 1, 2026' and 'Complete the 2027-2028 CSS Profile' -- one full year later, matching the currently-open admissions cycle. Separately: this page's own self-displayed 'last updated' date read 'Wednesday, May 5, 2027' at fetch time (2026-08-21) -- a date in the future relative to retrieval, almost certainly a templating artifact from an auto-incremented year-over-year clone of the prior cycle's page (which read 'Tuesday, May 5, 2026') rather than a real edit event; page 'updated' timestamps on this subdomain should not be trusted at face value without a sanity check against the retrieval date.

requirement_text: Financial aid at Columbia is need-based; there are no academic, athletic or talent-based institutional scholarships. ... Our need-based aid is in the form of grants and student work only. Loans are not used to meet financial need or included in initial financial aid awards.
researcher_notes: Per research-brief instruction: this is need-based aid, not a merit scholarship -- there is no merit-scholarship program at Columbia to confuse it with. Applies identically regardless of Early Decision vs Regular Decision admission (separately confirmed on the Myths About Financial Aid page: 'we will meet 100% of your demonstrated financial need, regardless of whether you were admitted early decision or regular decision').

requirement_text: If admitted, you must withdraw all other applications and accept our offer of admission. Only students who, after consultation with Financial Aid and Educational Financing, cite financial reasons for not attending will be released from the Early Decision agreement. ... According to the National Association for College Admission Counseling guidelines, “it is unethical… to have more than one pending Early Decision application.” While Columbia does not necessarily encourage the filing of both Early Decision (binding) and Early Action (non-binding) applications, we do not prohibit candidates from doing so. However, candidates should be aware that Columbia's Early Decision program is a binding agreement and a candidate will be expected to enroll, regardless of any pending applications (early or otherwise). ... If you are denied under the Early Decision plan, you must consider carefully your other college options. You may not apply to Columbia (Columbia College, Columbia Engineering or the School of General Studies) again for that year.
researcher_notes: This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact -- should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review to represent correctly. Additional mechanics from the same source page: deferred ED applicants join the Regular Decision pool and are notified by April 1, and are NOT obligated to enroll if later admitted through Regular Decision (asymmetric with the binding admit outcome); the only stated release valve from the binding agreement is demonstrated financial hardship after consultation with Financial Aid.

requirement_text: Columbia College and Columbia Engineering offer only one binding Early Decision round for first-year applicants (deadline November 1). No separate 'Early Decision II' round exists for these two schools; the official Dates & Deadlines table on the First-Year Applicants page and the dedicated Early Decision page each enumerate only Early Decision (November 1) and Regular Decision (January 1), with no second early round.
researcher_notes: CORRECTION TO RESEARCH BRIEF: the task brief for this research pass asserted that Columbia offers both Early Decision and Early Decision II. That is not supported by Columbia's own official pages -- both the First-Year Applicants Dates & Deadlines table (https://undergrad.admissions.columbia.edu/apply/firstyear) and the dedicated Early Decision page (https://undergrad.admissions.columbia.edu/apply/firstyear/early-decision) were fetched directly and each lists exactly one binding early round (Early Decision, Nov 1), with Regular Decision (Jan 1) as the only other track; the Early Decision page's own 'In This Section' index (Early Decision / QuestBridge / The Columbia-Juilliard Program / Homeschooled Applicants) does not include an ED II entry either. A web search surfaced third-party aggregator claims of a Columbia 'ED II' deadline of 'January 1' -- that figure is identical to Columbia's separately, officially published Regular Decision deadline, strongly suggesting those secondary sources mislabel Regular Decision as 'ED II' or conflate Columbia with a peer institution that does offer split ED I/ED II rounds. This finding should be treated as authoritative over the brief's premise; no ED II deadline or requirement record has been created for Columbia. (Note: Columbia's School of General Studies -- a separate school for nontraditional-age students, out of scope for this first-year Columbia College / Columbia Engineering research -- has its own distinct admission cycle structure and was not investigated here; it is not the source of the ED II claim since GS is not what the brief or this research targets.)
